name: C0 · Corpus KPIs
description: KPI strip: live documents, banks, doc types, undated, soft-deleted and the date span of the corpus — the header context every other card is read against.
sql:
-- Corpus KPIs
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE d.deleted_at IS NULL)                       AS live_documents,
       count(DISTINCT d.source_code) FILTER (WHERE d.deleted_at IS NULL)  AS banks,
       count(DISTINCT d.doc_type)    FILTER (WHERE d.deleted_at IS NULL)  AS doc_types,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE d.deleted_at IS NULL AND d.date IS NULL)    AS undated,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE d.deleted_at IS NOT NULL)                   AS soft_deleted,
       min(d.date) FILTER (WHERE d.deleted_at IS NULL)                    AS oldest,
       max(d.date) FILTER (WHERE d.deleted_at IS NULL)                    AS newest
FROM documents d
WHERE d.corpus = {{corpus}};

name: C1 · Documents by year
description: Documents published per year (inventory #4, #2); undated rows are dropped here by construction and counted separately by C0.
sql:
-- Documents by year
SELECT d.year AS year,
       count(*) AS documents
FROM documents d
WHERE d.deleted_at IS NULL
  AND d.corpus = {{corpus}}
  AND d.year IS NOT NULL
  [[AND d.source_code = {{bank}}]]
  [[AND d.doc_type = {{doc_type}}]]
  [[AND (d.date IS NULL OR d.date <= {{as_of}})]]
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;

name: C2 · Documents by group (A–G)
description: Documents per taxonomy group (inventory #4); the group letters are inlined as a VALUES list so an empty group renders as a zero bar instead of vanishing.
sql:
-- Documents by taxonomy group
WITH groups (group_letter, group_label) AS (
    VALUES ('A', 'Monetary policy — decisions & deliberation'),
           ('B', 'Press conferences & transcripts'),
           ('C', 'Speeches & interviews'),
           ('D', 'Research'),
           ('E', 'Reports'),
           ('F', 'Projections'),
           ('G', 'Supervisory / statistical')
)
SELECT g.group_letter,
       g.group_label,
       count(d.doc_id) AS documents
FROM groups g
LEFT JOIN documents d
       ON left(d.doc_type, 1) = g.group_letter
      AND d.deleted_at IS NULL
      AND d.corpus = {{corpus}}
      [[AND d.source_code = {{bank}}]]
      [[AND (d.date IS NULL OR d.date <= {{as_of}})]]
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1;

name: C3 · Cumulative corpus over time
description: Monthly and cumulative document counts (inventory #4); the one card that drops undated documents on purpose — a cumulative curve cannot place them.
sql:
-- Cumulative corpus over time
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('month', d.date)::date AS month,
           count(*) AS documents
    FROM documents d
    WHERE d.deleted_at IS NULL
      AND d.corpus = {{corpus}}
      AND d.date IS NOT NULL
      [[AND d.date <= {{as_of}}]]
      [[AND d.source_code = {{bank}}]]
      [[AND d.doc_type = {{doc_type}}]]
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT month,
       documents,
       sum(documents) OVER (ORDER BY month
                            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
           AS cumulative_documents
FROM monthly
ORDER BY month;

name: C4 · Document explorer (with RAG state)
description: Browsable document table with the official link and RAG state (inventory #3, #5, #2); rag_state any/in/out replaces the Streamlit "only in the RAG" toggle. Keep the LIMIT — the file download stays `vaultctl download <doc_id>`.
sql:
-- Documents with RAG state
SELECT d.doc_id,
       d.source_code   AS bank,
       d.doc_type      AS type,
       d.date,
       d.title,
       (r.doc_id IS NOT NULL) AS in_rag,
       r.chunk_count   AS n_chunks,
       r.embedding_model,
       r.ingested_at   AS rag_ingested_at,
       coalesce(d.pdf_url, d.source_url) AS official_link,
       d.page_count,
       d.has_text_layer
FROM documents d
LEFT JOIN rag_ingestions r
       ON r.doc_id = d.doc_id
      AND r.collection = {{collection}}
WHERE d.deleted_at IS NULL
  AND d.corpus = {{corpus}}
  [[AND ({{rag_state}} = 'any'
       OR ({{rag_state}} = 'in'  AND r.doc_id IS NOT NULL)
       OR ({{rag_state}} = 'out' AND r.doc_id IS NULL))]]
  [[AND (d.date IS NULL OR d.date <= {{as_of}})]]
  [[AND d.source_code = {{bank}}]]
  [[AND d.doc_type = {{doc_type}}]]
ORDER BY d.date DESC NULLS LAST, d.doc_id
LIMIT 2000;

name: C5 · Inventory per bank × doc_type
description: One row per (bank, type) series with total, active span, average and median per year (inventory #6); the median is zero-filled over the active span and `empty_years` makes that zero-filling visible.
sql:
-- Inventory per bank x doc_type
WITH scoped AS (
    SELECT d.source_code, d.doc_type, d.year
    FROM documents d
    WHERE d.deleted_at IS NULL
      AND d.corpus = {{corpus}}
      AND d.year IS NOT NULL
      [[AND d.source_code = {{bank}}]]
      [[AND (d.date IS NULL OR d.date <= {{as_of}})]]
), yearly AS (
    SELECT source_code, doc_type, year, count(*)::int AS n
    FROM scoped GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
), span AS (
    SELECT source_code, doc_type,
           min(year) AS first_year, max(year) AS last_year, sum(n)::int AS total
    FROM yearly GROUP BY 1, 2
), filled AS (
    SELECT s.source_code, s.doc_type, gs.year::int AS year, coalesce(y.n, 0) AS n
    FROM span s
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL generate_series(s.first_year, s.last_year) AS gs(year)
    LEFT JOIN yearly y
           ON y.source_code = s.source_code
          AND y.doc_type   = s.doc_type
          AND y.year       = gs.year
)
SELECT s.source_code AS bank,
       s.doc_type    AS type,
       s.total       AS documents,
       s.first_year,
       s.last_year,
       (s.last_year - s.first_year + 1) AS active_years,
       round(s.total::numeric / (s.last_year - s.first_year + 1), 2) AS avg_per_year,
       percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY f.n) AS median_per_year,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE f.n = 0) AS empty_years
FROM span s
JOIN filled f
  ON f.source_code = s.source_code AND f.doc_type = s.doc_type
GROUP BY s.source_code, s.doc_type, s.total, s.first_year, s.last_year
ORDER BY s.source_code, s.doc_type;

name: C6 · Coverage matrix year × doc_type
description: Pivot-ready year × type × documents (inventory #7); kept as three long columns so a new doc_type appears on its own. Run it with a bank filter.
sql:
-- Coverage matrix year x doc_type (pivot-ready)
SELECT d.year AS year,
       d.doc_type AS type,
       count(*) AS documents
FROM documents d
WHERE d.deleted_at IS NULL
  AND d.corpus = {{corpus}}
  AND d.year IS NOT NULL
  [[AND d.source_code = {{bank}}]]
  [[AND (d.date IS NULL OR d.date <= {{as_of}})]]
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2;

name: Q1 · Publication anomalies
description: Missing / low / exceptional yearly volume per (bank, type) against a zero-filled non-zero median baseline (inventory #9); all six knobs are parameters, not constants.
sql:
-- Publication anomalies (missing / low / exceptional yearly volume)
WITH params AS (
    SELECT coalesce(NULL::date [[, {{ref_date}}]], current_date) AS as_of,
           {{window_years}}::int    AS window_years,
           {{min_nonzero_years}}::int AS min_nonzero_years,
           {{min_baseline}}::numeric  AS min_baseline,
           {{low_ratio}}::numeric     AS low_ratio,
           {{high_ratio}}::numeric    AS high_ratio
), win AS (
    SELECT (extract(year FROM as_of)::int - 1)             AS y_to,
           (extract(year FROM as_of)::int - window_years)   AS y_from,
           min_nonzero_years, min_baseline, low_ratio, high_ratio
    FROM params
), yearly AS (
    SELECT d.source_code, d.doc_type, d.year, count(*)::int AS n
    FROM documents d
    WHERE d.deleted_at IS NULL
      AND d.corpus = {{corpus}}
      AND d.year IS NOT NULL
      [[AND d.source_code = {{bank}}]]
    GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
), span AS (
    SELECT source_code, doc_type, min(year) AS y_start, max(year) AS y_end
    FROM yearly GROUP BY 1, 2
), grid AS (
    SELECT s.source_code, s.doc_type, gs.year::int AS year
    FROM span s CROSS JOIN win w
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL generate_series(greatest(s.y_start, w.y_from),
                                       least(s.y_end,   w.y_to)) AS gs(year)
), counts AS (
    SELECT g.source_code, g.doc_type, g.year, coalesce(y.n, 0) AS n
    FROM grid g
    LEFT JOIN yearly y
           ON y.source_code = g.source_code
          AND y.doc_type    = g.doc_type
          AND y.year        = g.year
), baseline AS (
    SELECT source_code, doc_type,
           percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY n)
               FILTER (WHERE n > 0)              AS baseline,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE n > 0)::int    AS nonzero_years,
           count(*)::int                         AS years_considered
    FROM counts GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT c.source_code AS bank,
       c.doc_type    AS type,
       c.year,
       c.n           AS documents,
       round(b.baseline::numeric, 1) AS baseline_per_year,
       b.nonzero_years,
       round((100.0 * c.n / nullif(b.baseline, 0))::numeric, 0) AS pct_of_baseline,
       CASE WHEN c.n = 0                          THEN 'missing'
            WHEN c.n < w.low_ratio  * b.baseline  THEN 'low'
            WHEN c.n > w.high_ratio * b.baseline  THEN 'exceptional'
       END AS anomaly
FROM counts c
JOIN baseline b
  ON b.source_code = c.source_code AND b.doc_type = c.doc_type
CROSS JOIN win w
WHERE b.nonzero_years >= w.min_nonzero_years
  AND b.baseline      >= w.min_baseline
  AND (c.n = 0
       OR c.n < w.low_ratio  * b.baseline
       OR c.n > w.high_ratio * b.baseline)
ORDER BY c.source_code, c.doc_type, c.year;

name: Q2 · Upcoming & overdue
description: The watchdog's cadence snapshot for every (bank, type) series it knows (inventory #10). `snapshot_at` is surfaced as a column: cadence is a full-replace snapshot and stale data does not look stale.
sql:
-- Upcoming & overdue publications
SELECT c.source_code AS bank,
       c.doc_type    AS type,
       c.status,
       c.last        AS last_seen,
       c.interval_days,
       c.next_expected,
       c.days_until,
       c.expected_per_year,
       c.n_3y        AS docs_last_3y,
       c.updated_at  AS snapshot_at
FROM cadence c
WHERE c.corpus = {{corpus}}
  [[AND c.source_code = {{bank}}]]
  [[AND c.status = {{status}}]]
ORDER BY CASE c.status WHEN 'overdue' THEN 0 WHEN 'soon' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END,
         c.days_until NULLS LAST,
         c.source_code, c.doc_type;

name: Q3 · Expected vs observed per year
description: Data-driven replacement for the hard-coded EXPECTED_PER_YEAR calendar (inventory #8): cadence's expectation against the last 3 years actually recorded. A triage list, not a verdict.
sql:
-- Expected vs observed publication rate
WITH params AS (
    SELECT coalesce(NULL::date [[, {{ref_date}}]], current_date) AS as_of
), observed AS (
    SELECT d.source_code, d.doc_type,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE d.date >= (p.as_of - INTERVAL '3 years'))::numeric / 3.0
               AS observed_per_year_3y
    FROM documents d
    CROSS JOIN params p
    WHERE d.deleted_at IS NULL
      AND d.corpus = {{corpus}}
      AND d.date IS NOT NULL
      AND d.date <= p.as_of
    GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT c.source_code AS bank,
       c.doc_type    AS type,
       c.expected_per_year,
       round(coalesce(o.observed_per_year_3y, 0), 2) AS observed_per_year_3y,
       round(coalesce(o.observed_per_year_3y, 0) - c.expected_per_year, 2) AS gap,
       c.status
FROM cadence c
LEFT JOIN observed o
       ON o.source_code = c.source_code AND o.doc_type = c.doc_type
WHERE c.corpus = {{corpus}}
  [[AND c.source_code = {{bank}}]]
ORDER BY gap ASC NULLS LAST;

name: Q4 · RAG backlog by bank × type
description: Documents in the vault but not in the target collection, read from the `rag_backlog` view (inventory #3, inverse side); `needs_ocr` / `not_probed` make it double as the OCR work queue. Backlog 0 with C0's live_documents 0 means "no data", not "done".
sql:
-- RAG backlog: documents in the vault but not in the target collection
SELECT b.source_code AS bank,
       b.doc_type    AS type,
       count(*)                                          AS backlog_documents,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE b.has_text_layer IS FALSE) AS needs_ocr,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE b.has_text_layer IS NULL)  AS not_probed,
       min(b.date)   AS oldest,
       max(b.date)   AS newest
FROM rag_backlog b
WHERE b.corpus = {{corpus}}
  AND b.collection = {{collection}}
  [[AND b.source_code = {{bank}}]]
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY backlog_documents DESC;

name: Q5 · Fetching problems
description: Open discovery failures grouped by bank × context × error class (inventory #11), de-duplicated by fingerprint with `attempts` = summed occurrences.
sql:
-- Open fetching problems (discovery failures)
SELECT e.source_code AS bank,
       e.context,
       e.error_class,
       count(*)              AS distinct_urls,
       sum(e.occurrences)    AS attempts,
       max(e.last_seen_at)   AS last_seen,
       min(e.first_seen_at)  AS first_seen,
       (array_agg(e.url   ORDER BY e.last_seen_at DESC))[1] AS sample_url,
       (array_agg(e.error ORDER BY e.last_seen_at DESC))[1] AS sample_error
FROM discovery_errors e
WHERE e.corpus = {{corpus}}
  AND e.resolved_at IS NULL
  AND e.last_seen_at >= now() - ({{lookback_days}} || ' days')::interval
  [[AND e.source_code = {{bank}}]]
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
ORDER BY attempts DESC, last_seen DESC;

name: R1 · Chunks by collection
description: Documents and chunks recorded as ingested per collection and embedding model (inventory #1). Accepted loss: this is the vault's belief, not live Qdrant state.
sql:
-- Chunks by collection
SELECT r.collection,
       r.embedding_model,
       r.embedding_version,
       count(*)                     AS documents_ingested,
       sum(r.chunk_count)           AS chunks,
       round(avg(r.chunk_count), 1) AS avg_chunks_per_doc,
       max(r.ingested_at)           AS last_ingested_at
FROM rag_ingestions r
WHERE r.corpus = {{corpus}}
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
ORDER BY chunks DESC;

name: R2 · RAG coverage by bank × type
description: How far along the RAG ingestion is per (bank, type) (inventory #3). Q4 answers "what is left"; this answers "how far along".
sql:
-- RAG coverage per bank x type
SELECT d.source_code AS bank,
       d.doc_type    AS type,
       count(*)                                     AS documents,
       count(r.doc_id)                              AS in_rag,
       count(*) - count(r.doc_id)                   AS missing_from_rag,
       round(100.0 * count(r.doc_id) / count(*), 1) AS pct_in_rag,
       coalesce(sum(r.chunk_count), 0)              AS chunks
FROM documents d
LEFT JOIN rag_ingestions r
       ON r.doc_id = d.doc_id
      AND r.collection = {{collection}}
WHERE d.deleted_at IS NULL
  AND d.corpus = {{corpus}}
  [[AND d.source_code = {{bank}}]]
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY pct_in_rag ASC, documents DESC;

name: R3 · Last run per tool
description: The most recent run of every producer with its totals and `age` — the silent-failure detector: a nightly tool whose last run is 3 days old is broken even when `outcome` says ok.
sql:
-- Last run per tool
SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.tool)
       r.tool,
       r.command,
       r.outcome,
       r.exit_code,
       r.started_at,
       r.finished_at,
       round(extract(epoch FROM (r.finished_at - r.started_at))::numeric / 60.0, 1) AS minutes,
       (r.totals ->> 'docs_seen')::int          AS docs_seen,
       coalesce((r.totals ->> 'docs_ingested')::int,
                (r.totals ->> 'docs_new')::int) AS docs_ingested,
       (r.totals ->> 'docs_failed')::int        AS docs_failed,
       (r.totals ->> 'docs_path_metadata')::int AS docs_path_metadata,
       jsonb_array_length(coalesce(r.sources, '[]'::jsonb)) AS n_sources,
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM jsonb_array_elements(coalesce(r.sources, '[]'::jsonb)) s
               WHERE (s ->> 'truncated')::boolean) AS any_truncated,
       now() - r.finished_at                     AS age
FROM runs r
ORDER BY r.tool, r.finished_at DESC NULLS LAST;

name: R4 · Degraded / failed streaks
description: Gaps-and-islands over consecutive non-ok runs per tool: one bad night is noise, four in a row is an incident, and this card tells them apart.
sql:
-- Consecutive non-ok run streaks per tool
WITH ordered AS (
    SELECT r.tool, r.run_id, r.command, r.outcome, r.exit_code, r.finished_at,
           (r.outcome IS DISTINCT FROM 'ok') AS bad,
           row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY r.tool ORDER BY r.finished_at) AS rn,
           row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY r.tool, (r.outcome IS DISTINCT FROM 'ok')
                              ORDER BY r.finished_at) AS rn_bad
    FROM runs r
    WHERE r.finished_at IS NOT NULL
      AND r.finished_at >= now() - ({{lookback_days}} || ' days')::interval
), islands AS (
    SELECT *, rn - rn_bad AS grp FROM ordered
)
SELECT tool,
       count(*)                                            AS run_count,
       min(finished_at)                                    AS streak_start,
       max(finished_at)                                    AS streak_end,
       string_agg(DISTINCT outcome, ', ' ORDER BY outcome) AS outcomes,
       max(exit_code)                                      AS worst_exit_code
FROM islands
WHERE bad
GROUP BY tool, grp
HAVING count(*) >= {{min_streak}}
ORDER BY streak_end DESC, run_count DESC;

name: R5 · Path-metadata trend
description: Share of ingested documents whose metadata came from the file path rather than the manifest, per day and tool — a rising share is a silent quality regression. `totals ? 'docs_path_metadata'` excludes runs from before the key existed.
sql:
-- Documents whose metadata came from the path, per day
SELECT date_trunc('day', r.finished_at)::date AS day,
       r.tool,
       count(*)                                      AS runs,
       sum((r.totals ->> 'docs_path_metadata')::int) AS docs_path_metadata,
       sum(coalesce((r.totals ->> 'docs_ingested')::int,
                    (r.totals ->> 'docs_new')::int)) AS docs_ingested,
       round(100.0 * sum((r.totals ->> 'docs_path_metadata')::int)
             / nullif(sum(coalesce((r.totals ->> 'docs_ingested')::int,
                                   (r.totals ->> 'docs_new')::int)), 0), 1)
                                                     AS pct_path_metadata
FROM runs r
WHERE r.totals ? 'docs_path_metadata'
  AND r.finished_at >= now() - ({{lookback_days}} || ' days')::interval
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1 DESC, 2;

name: R6 · Truncated sources
description: Runs whose per-source listing stopped early (`truncated: true`) with the fetch-error counters and error samples — without this card the honest-discovery flag is invisible.
sql:
-- Runs whose per-source listing was truncated
SELECT r.tool,
       r.command,
       r.finished_at,
       r.outcome,
       s ->> 'source_code'          AS source_code,
       (s ->> 'docs_seen')::int     AS docs_seen,
       (s ->> 'docs_new')::int      AS docs_new,
       (s ->> 'docs_failed')::int   AS docs_failed,
       (s ->> 'fetch_errors')::int  AS fetch_errors,
       (s -> 'error_samples')       AS error_samples
FROM runs r
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(coalesce(r.sources, '[]'::jsonb)) AS s
WHERE (s ->> 'truncated')::boolean IS TRUE
  AND r.finished_at >= now() - ({{lookback_days}} || ' days')::interval
ORDER BY r.finished_at DESC, source_code;
